title: Why bond prices and yields move in opposite directions
researchPrompt: A bond pays a fixed coupon. Explain why its market price falls when prevailing interest rates rise, and why that relationship is arithmetic rather than sentiment.
suggestedAngles: Start from a single fixed coupon and ask what a buyer would pay once better rates exist elsewhere
Frame it as competition between an old contract and a new one
Use duration to explain why long-dated bonds swing harder than short-dated ones

title: Comparative advantage
researchPrompt: Explain why two countries both gain from trade even when one is better at producing everything. Make the counterintuitive part land.
suggestedAngles: Use opportunity cost rather than absolute productivity as the unit of comparison
Shrink it to two people in one office deciding who does which task
Address the intuitive objection head-on: being better at everything still leaves gains on the table

title: The Jevons paradox
researchPrompt: Efficiency improvements can increase total consumption of the resource they save. Explain the mechanism, then explain when it does not hold.
suggestedAngles: Trace the causal chain: efficiency lowers effective price, lower price raises demand
Separate the direct rebound effect from the economy-wide one
Argue the limiting case: what has to be true for efficiency to genuinely reduce use
